summary: Three levels: an app in one workspace (no review), unlisted public distribution (self-serve checklist), and Slack Marketplace listing (reviewed). Know which you need before starting.

difficulty.label: Review required
difficulty.rationale: A single-workspace app is instant, but a commercial app that other companies install belongs on the Marketplace: it needs 10 active workspaces first, then a two-part manual review, and non-Marketplace commercial apps get stricter API rate limits.

effort.basis: Our estimate: creating the app is quick, building and securing an OAuth flow with SSL URLs takes longer. No source states a time.

wait.statement: Slack states maximums, not typical times: up to 10 business days for the preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks for the functional review of a new submission (6 weeks for resubmitted published apps). Our sum is about 12 weeks. Slack says turnaround varies with volume. Unlisted distribution and single-workspace apps have no review.

composio_managed.note: Composio's Slack guide says managed auth is available: 'Composio provides the Slack app, so there's nothing to configure.' Use your own app only for custom branding, scopes or control.

requirements.text: To activate public distribution you must complete a checklist, including SSL on OAuth redirect, interactivity, select-options and Events API URLs.
You need an onboarding flow, since the user base can grow quickly.
Before submitting you need at least 10 installations on active workspaces, and Slack says to keep 10 or more installed through the whole review.
An active workspace is one used in the past 28 days.

scopes_and_access.text: Request only the permissions the app truly needs; workspace admins weigh them during approval.

gotchas.text: Deactivating public distribution removes the app from every workspace that installed it except the original one.
After publishing in the Marketplace you cannot disable distribution the same way; you must discontinue the listing.
Composio's page lists a separate custom-app guide (composio.dev/auth/slack_custom) for your own Slack app; the main Slack guide gives no custom steps.
Slack applies reduced rate limits to newly created commercially distributed apps that are not Marketplace-approved (effective May 29, 2025). The page we read does not give the numbers.
Preliminary review resets your place in the queue each time you resubmit; the functional review does not.

steps.title: Decide: managed or your own app
steps.detail: For prototyping use Composio Managed Auth (connect, pick workspace, Allow). Create your own app for custom branding, scopes or a dedicated quota.
steps.why_not_agent: A product decision about branding and control.

steps.title: Create the Slack app and install it in your own workspace
steps.detail: Install App to Workspace gives one token for that workspace, no OAuth code needed.
steps.why_not_agent: Needs your signed-in Slack admin session.

steps.title: Build the OAuth flow if other workspaces need access
steps.detail: Needed for acting on behalf of other users or installing elsewhere. Composio handles this when you use its auth config with your own credentials.

steps.title: Enable distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution > Share Your App with Other Workspaces > complete the checklist > Activate Public Distribution. Suitable for pilots.
steps.why_not_agent: Needs your Slack app dashboard session and legal/security decisions.

steps.title: For commercial distribution, submit to the Marketplace
steps.detail: Slack reviews listed apps against its requirements and guidelines.
steps.why_not_agent: Submission and review communication are yours.

blockers.likely_cause: Checklist incomplete, e.g. a required URL is not served over SSL.
blockers.fix: Make every listed URL HTTPS and complete the checklist items.
blockers.escalate_when: Checklist is complete but activation stays disabled.

review_process.text: Review has automated tests, then a manual review in two parts: preliminary (is the app ready) and functional (installation and testing).
Preliminary feedback takes up to 10 business days; functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions and 6 weeks for resubmitted published apps.

next_actions: If prototyping: use managed auth now.
If you need your own app: create it, install to your workspace, then decide whether unlisted or Marketplace fits.

agent_can: Walk the distribution checklist and verify your URLs are HTTPS.

The rate-limit page points to a changelog for the exact limits; the per-minute number was not read.
Slack's app-creation click path was not read; follow Slack's current docs.
How a team gets its first 10 active workspaces without being listed (unlisted distribution) is not detailed in the pages read.
